title: Linux release (CGO-off) builds cannot resolve .local mDNS endpoints; reported as 'server offline'
description:
Released binaries cannot resolve mDNS `.local` hosts, and the failure is reported as "server offline".

## Symptom
With `endpoint: http://Apollo-II.local:1111`, the Homebrew v0.23.0 binary refuses to send:

    cannot send — server offline (http://Apollo-II.local:1111): apogee: model discovery:
    Get "http://Apollo-II.local:1111/v1/models": dial tcp: lookup Apollo-II.local on
    100.100.100.100:53: no such host

The server is up: `getent hosts Apollo-II.local` → `192.168.0.55`.

## Cause
`make dist` builds every release archive with `CGO_ENABLED=0` (Makefile, dist target), so the Homebrew binary uses Go's pure-Go resolver. It cannot load NSS modules, so `hosts: files mdns4_minimal [NOTFOUND=return] dns` never reaches avahi. The query goes to the unicast nameserver in /etc/resolv.conf (Tailscale MagicDNS, 100.100.100.100), which returns NXDOMAIN.
A local `make build` binary (native, CGO_ENABLED=1) uses the cgo resolver and works. That is why it "worked earlier today": `~/.apogee/server-stats.jsonl` shows successful Apollo-II requests at 10:12Z from `./apogee`, and the failure appeared after switching to the brew v0.23.0 binary.

## Regression status
This is not a code regression. The dist target has used CGO_ENABLED=0 since it was added, so brew v0.22.x and earlier would fail the same way on this host. It regressed from the user's point of view: the same config works with a source build and fails with the shipped build.

## Two defects
1. **Resolution:** shipped binaries cannot reach `.local` (mDNS) endpoints on Linux (and likely macOS, depending on the Go version's darwin resolver path), which is a common way to address a LAN LLM box.
2. **Diagnosis:** a DNS lookup failure is presented as "server offline". It should say that the host name did not resolve, and hint at `/etc/hosts` or the IP for `.local` names.

## Workarounds
Use the IP in the endpoint, or add `192.168.0.55 Apollo-II.local` to /etc/hosts (the pure-Go resolver reads it).

## Fix directions (to design)
- Resolve `.local` names in apogee itself via a small mDNS query (multicast 224.0.0.251:5353) when the system lookup fails, so CGO_ENABLED=0 builds keep working.
- Or ship cgo-enabled Linux/macOS builds (hard for cross-compiled `make dist`).
- Either way, classify `*net.DNSError` separately from connection-refused in the offline/probe message.
acceptance_criteria: A release-built (CGO_ENABLED=0) apogee reaches an endpoint named <host>.local that the OS resolves via mDNS; a DNS lookup failure is reported as an unresolved host name, not 'server offline'; both pinned by tests.
notes: 2026-09-24: confirmed Linux-only. The same brew binary works on macOS: since Go 1.20, darwin builds call libSystem's resolver even with CGO_ENABLED=0, and that resolver handles mDNS. On Linux the pure-Go resolver cannot load NSS (mdns4_minimal), so it queries unicast DNS only. It hits any Linux host running a release build whose LLM server is addressed by an mDNS-only .local name. Source builds (make build, CGO on) are unaffected.

title: Sub-agent shown as done before it finishes
description:
Sub-agents are sometimes shown as "done" (✓) even though they have not finished and have not submitted their final report. The owner sees it now and then.

## Diagnosis (2026-09-24, read-only; no repro yet)

The engine side is sound. `runDelegation` (internal/agent/dispatch.go:777) emits SubAgentFinished only after runSubAgent returns, and events reach the TUI in order (sink.go:95, bridge.go:205). The UI pairs events by call id alone, and nothing makes call ids unique across the delegation tree.

### Candidate causes, most likely first

1. **Call-id collision in a parallel fan-out (HIGH).** At width > 1, dispatchGroup (dispatch.go:363) emits every head's ToolCallEvent before any child runs. `place` (transcript.go:486) then inserts child A's inner calls inside A's span, ahead of sibling head B. `addToolResult` (internal/tui/transcript.go:1517) pairs a result with the newest open entry whose `callID` matches and checks neither depth nor spawn id. So if an inner call of A has the same id as B's head, A's leaf result closes B's head (`e.done = true`). `delegationVerdict` (toolregistry.go:906) then labels it `done` and B shows ✓ while its child is still running.
   Ids collide in two ways:
   - Salvage ids `text_call_<turnIndex>_<i>` (builtins.go:265). The child's turn index restarts at 0 (construct.go:162), so a child at turn T that salvages two or more calls produces `text_call_T_1`, which is the second head's id.
   - Native per-reply counter ids (`call_0`, `call_1`) from some local servers or chat templates.

   It needs width > 1 and non-unique ids, which is why it is intermittent. It never happens on Anthropic, whose `toolu_` ids are unique.
2. **Duplicate sub_agent ids within one reply (MEDIUM-HIGH).** Nothing removes duplicate ids from a reply (children.go:46 acknowledges this: ADR 0059 §6). The first child's SubAgentFinished reaches `addSubAgentPhase` (transcript.go:1599, also `headsRunFor` :2108), which matches by callID and ticks the last head with that id. The two runs also merge under one head. With delegate-max-depth ≥ 2, a grandchild's spawn id can collide the same way.
3. **The child really ended, but not on a report (MEDIUM).** A child ends on any reply that has text and no tool call. `completedResult` (subagent.go:1846) does not run the narration check (`closingShapeOf`/`endsOnIntent`, subagent.go:342); that check runs only on the step-capped path. So a delegate that stops on "Let me now read X." counts as its report and shows ✓ done. `noReportMarker` "[delegate returned no report]" (subagent.go:268) also shows ✓ done. apogee-2h6 and apogee-1zz closed this gap for the capped path only.
4. **"finished before your message landed" is wrong wording (LOW).** `drainMailbox` → `reportUndelivered` (children.go:480) fires when Interject refuses. transcript.go:1667 always words that as "finished", even though the child is still running.

### Telling them apart
- Look at the parent's sub_agent call ids in the affected session:
  - `text_call_…` or `call_0`/`call_1`-style ids point to #1.
  - The same id on two sub_agent calls point to #2.
  - Unique ids leave #3.
- Look at the row that ticked early:
  - A leaf tool's output (file text, a grep hit) in its body points to #1.
  - A "Let me …" narration or "[delegate returned no report]" points to #3.

### Proposed tests
- #1: a transcript test. Send two depth-0 heads c0 and c1, then a depth-1 ToolCallEvent and ToolResultEvent with spawn c0 and Call.ID c1. Assert that head c1 is not done. This is expected to fail today.
- #2: two heads with id c0 and one SubAgentFinished{c0}.
- #3: a stub-LLM delegate whose last reply is narration with no tool call.

### Fix direction
- UI: pair results and phases by full run identity (depth plus spawn id, checking the entry's spawnCallID), not by callID alone.
- Engine: make ids unique per Agent and per reply. That means a per-agent prefix for synthesised `text_call_` ids, and deduplicating repeated native ids in a way that does not break the dispatchableCalls rule that native ids are never made up.
- #3: extend the narration check to the completed path, or show "stopped without a report" separately from "done".

Related: apogee-2un (open; nearby, not the cause).
close_reason: Plan 2026-09-24 - 01 landed all 8 items; the two deferred gaps are fixed in 3e1234af (record closes a tool call in its own run) and a02fb5ad (SubAgentUsage bracketed by run id). Sessions saved before item 6 still replay a no-report delegation as done: no verdict was recorded, so none can be recovered.

title: Copy never reaches the clipboard when apogee runs inside tmux
description: Drag-select copy flashes 'copied N chars' but nothing pastes when apogee runs inside tmux on its default set-clipboard external (e.g. VS Code remote terminal profile running tmux over SSH). tmux 3.5a input_osc_52 drops an application's OSC 52 unless set-clipboard is on; the atotto system-clipboard fallback writes the remote host's clipboard (no DISPLAY). Verified 2026-09-23: a program's \e]52 is dropped under 'external', while 'tmux load-buffer -w -' reaches the attached client as OSC 52. Fix: when TMUX is set, copyFlash also hands the text to 'tmux load-buffer -w -'. Tests only assert a non-nil Cmd + flash; nothing asserts the OSC 52 bytes on the wire. Workaround: tmux set -g set-clipboard on.
close_reason: Resolved by plan 2026-09-23 - 00 - tmux-copy-route-plan (archived a17ae6e2): copy inside tmux also pipes to tmux load-buffer -w; driven test pins OSC 52 bytes

title: undo: a chat-only exchange re-closes the previous group, clearing redo and absorbing human edits
description:
Found by the regression check of 'docs/plans/2026-09-23 - 00 - slow-box-follow-ups-and-stale-state-plan.md' (2026-09-23). Not a regression: latent since ac9cbcf6 (feat(undo): snapshot-backed Exchange groups, v0.20.8); identical at v0.22.7 and before 9f684b83.
Journal.Close -> closeGroup (internal/undo/snapshot.go) never consults pending. An exchange that makes no write-capable tool call never reaches MarkPre/openGroup, so pending stays true (set by takeWalk or loop.go BeginGroup) and closeGroup acts on groups[len-1] — the PREVIOUS, already-closed group — re-capturing its post image and re-diffing against its pre.
Effects: (1) after /undo, any chat-only exchange with >=2 snapshotted groups finds a non-empty diff, sets j.redo = nil and bumps the generation — /redo is lost. (2) Even without undo, every chat-only exchange re-closes the previous group, so edits the human made between exchanges are absorbed into that group's post image and a later /undo reverts them too.
No test covers it (TestRedo_MaterialisedGroupClearsTheStack_BareBeginGroupDoesNot never calls Close). Candidate fix: Close is a no-op for the group when pending is true (no group opened this exchange) — confirm cancel/re-attempt paths never rely on re-closing.
close_reason: Item 10: an exchange that opened no group closes none; resolved by plan '2026-09-23 - 00 - slow-box-follow-ups-and-stale-state-plan' (archived at 152dc896)

title: The pre-commit secret scan silently skips itself after 2s
description:
internal/agent/secretsguard.go:40 commitSecretsTimeout = 2 * time.Second per git invocation, and on expiry the check is SKIPPED for that call. That is a security control that degrades off without saying so: two seconds covers a shadow-index `git add` over the call's files, but a large file set on a slow disk or a cold page cache exceeds it and the commit proceeds unscanned.

Contrast internal/agent/treesnapshot.go:32, the same 2s value, where the skip is deliberate and degrades a WARNING rather than a control.

Found by the slow-box deadline sweep, 2026-09-22.
acceptance_criteria: A scan that runs out of time is reported, not silently skipped; the budget is sized for a large repo on slow storage.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Airic Lenz
comments.text:
Verified fixed in the tree at 533ce9af (slow-box-deadlines plan, item 2, commit f090b515).

- internal/agent/secretsguard.go: commitSecretsTimeout 2s -> 30s, and it now bounds the WHOLE pre-check (one context covers all four shadow runs) rather than each git invocation.
- The silent skip on expiry is gone. The check has three outcomes instead of two, stated as a binding robustness contract in the package doc: (a) no repository to scan — still a silent skip, nothing to look at; (b) clean; (c) RESOLVED a repository and could not finish — errScanTimedOut / a mid-scan git failure now forces the Tier-2 approval look with incompleteScanReason in the audit trail and incompleteScanHint on the prompt's Fix row ('the staged-secret scan could not finish, so the staged content is unchecked'). The pre-check still never FAILS a commit the tool would have made; the worst it does is ask.
- That explicitly supersedes ADR 0080 decision 6 and ADR 0056 decision 4, whose blanket silent skip made a control that did not run indistinguishable from one that ran clean.
- Covered by new cases in internal/agent/secretsguard_test.go; the configuration manual gained the note.

Acceptance met on both halves: the incomplete scan is reported, and the budget fits a large index on slow storage.

title: Discovery's 5s timeout plus a 2-failure debounce paints a saturated local server offline and refuses the send
description:
internal/provider/discovery.go:15 discoveryTimeout = 5 * time.Second bounds the /v1/models probe. internal/heartbeat/heartbeat.go:31 Interval = 10s and internal/tui/heartbeat.go:130 offlineFailureThreshold = 2 turn two consecutive probe timeouts into the footeri reading `offline`, and internal/tui/model.go:3317-3318 makes offline the state a send is REFUSED in.

A single-slot llama.cpp/Ollama server mid-prefill on a throttled laptop routinely takes longer than 5s to answer any HTTP request — the ordinary case for this product, not an edge case. The comment at heartbeat.go:125-127 already names the failure ("discovery's own timeout can elapse on a server that is merely saturated") and answers it with the debounce rather than with a longer probe. Neither constant is configurable.

Found by the slow-box deadline sweep, 2026-09-22, alongside the handoff docs/handoffs/2026-09-22 - 00 - ci-and-test-failures-triage.md. The two are one bug, not two.
acceptance_criteria: A saturated local server that answers slowly is not painted offline and does not refuse a send; the probe budget is sized for slow local hardware (or made configurable).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Airic Lenz
comments.text:
Verified fixed in the tree at 533ce9af (slow-box-deadlines plan, item 1, commit 1ae96240).

- internal/provider/discovery.go: discoveryTimeout 5s -> exported DiscoveryTimeout = 30 * time.Second, with the reasoning recorded (the budget is only ever SPENT on a failure, so a generous one is free; a saturated single-slot server answers late, not never). WithDiscoveryTimeout is the override.
- internal/heartbeat/heartbeat.go: Interval is no longer a stated 10s but DERIVED — 'const Interval = 2 * provider.DiscoveryTimeout' (60s) — so 'a beat is strictly shorter than the interval' holds by construction.
- internal/tui/heartbeat.go: offlineFailureThreshold stays 2 deliberately, but the debounce window widened with the probe budget to ~2 minutes; the doc comment states that this is the price of not calling a saturated server dead.
- The send refusal on offline (internal/tui/model.go) is unchanged by design — what changed is that a slow-but-healthy server no longer reaches that state.
- Docs re-worded off 'ten-second heartbeat' in docs/manual/configuration.md, internal/config/config.go and internal/config/defaults/config.yaml.

Acceptance met by sizing rather than by a config key, which the acceptance allowed.

title: landlock/bwrap net-deny box leaves UDP and pathname-UNIX-socket egress open with no Residual disclosed (audit 2026-09-20 High)
description:
Source: docs/reviews/code-audit-2026-09-20.md, High 'a network-deny box does not fence UDP or pathname-UNIX-socket egress, and reports no Residual'.
Where: internal/platform/landlock_linux.go:298-311,199-222; internal/platform/namespace_linux.go:237-238.
What: landlock handles only LANDLOCK_ACCESS_NET_CONNECT_TCP; unhandled rights are unrestricted, so a confined child keeps UDP egress (DNS exfil on 53) and pathname-UNIX-socket egress (LANDLOCK_ACCESS_FS_RESOLVE_UNIX never handled). bwrap --unshare-net cuts UDP and abstract sockets but a pathname UNIX socket is filesystem-scoped: /var/run/docker.sock, /run/user/<uid>/bus stay reachable. Capabilities() reports NetworkEgress: true with empty Residuals — a capability-honesty violation (contract: every gap is disclosed, as the truncate gap is).
Audit fix: handle LANDLOCK_ACCESS_FS_RESOLVE_UNIX at ABI >= 9 and the UDP rights at ABI >= 10 when the box opts into deny; disclose whatever an ABI leaves open in Capabilities().Residuals; for bwrap disclose the residual and refuse the tightening or document it; add a confinetest row driving a UDP send under a net-deny box. The disclosure half is small and could ship first; the landlock rights half is the design.
close_reason: Plan 2026-09-22 - 00 items 6-9: landlock and bwrap net-deny boxes disclose the egress they cannot fence as Residuals; residual notice words each; confinetest UDP row (positive landlock arm tracked by apogee-ifrv).

title: present.command (rung-3 opener) runs a model-chosen program unapproved and unconfined in every mode (audit 2026-09-20 High)
description:
Source: docs/reviews/code-audit-2026-09-20.md, High 'the rung-3 opener (present.command) runs a model-chosen program unapproved and unconfined in every mode'.
Where: cmd/apogee/wire_present.go:58-65, internal/present/opener.go:194-198,387-412, internal/presenter.go:141-152.
What: with a Local session and auto-open on, present_document is ReadOnly, so rung 3's Opener.Open(req.Path) runs in every mode, Plan included, with no gate. argv[0] is PATH-resolved at exec with no writable-path fence (rung 1 goes through security.ResolveProgram), and {path} is model-chosen into the workspace: write a script under confinement, present_document it, 'sh {path}' runs it as the user. Below Critical only because present.command is a user-set, file-only global override.
Audit fix: resolve and fence rung 3's argv[0] through security.ResolveProgram as rung 1 does; gate the opener half of present_document through the disposition when an execution-capable rung is wired (classify as an external effect, or run the opener inside the session's Confiner box). ADR 0019 §5's 'user's own configuration' rationale predates the model-triggerable tool — revisit it in the design.
close_reason: Closed

title: .beads/hooks activation runs repo-shipped shell as live git hooks (audit 2026-09-20 Critical)
description:
Source: docs/reviews/code-audit-2026-09-20.md, Critical 'repo-shipped .beads/hooks/* become live git hooks with the user's full privileges'.
Where: .beads/hooks/commit-msg, post-checkout, pre-push, prepare-commit-msg — activated by bd init / bd hooks install pointing core.hooksPath at .beads/hooks (the documented hydration recipe in AGENTS.md).
What: committed, executable, repo-controlled shell; bd's marker handling preserves commit-msg (marker-free) and prepare-commit-msg's unmarked tail verbatim, so after hydration the next git commit/checkout/push runs the repo's shell as the user.
Audit fix: bd hooks install should only activate hooks it can vouch for (hash-pin the marked files, refuse or flag unmarked content), or the repo must not ship live hooks.
Repo-policy call for the owner (handoff 2026-09-21 step 4): this repo IS the owner's own — the hooks are the attribution stripper and the bd-init guard the owner wrote. Candidate outcomes: (a) won't-fix + document in SECURITY.md/AGENTS.md that hydration trusts the checkout's hooks and a clone of an untrusted fork must inspect .beads/hooks before bd hooks install; (b) upstream a hash-pin to bd. Not an apogee code change either way.
close_reason: Documented, not coded (owner call 2026-09-22): plan 2026-09-22 - 00 item 14 — SECURITY.md and AGENTS.md state what hook hydration trusts.

title: undo journal holds its mutex across filesystem writes (audit 2026-09-20 Critical)
description:
Source: docs/reviews/code-audit-2026-09-20.md, Critical 'the undo journal holds its mutex across filesystem writes' (internal/undo/journal.go Revert/runStep/entry.apply, snapshot.go tracked.apply). The whole revert/redo step — SafeWriteFile/SafeRemove plus blocking git reads in snapshot-backed groups — runs under j.mu, the lock Record/MarkPre/Close also take; a slow restore stalls the engine, a revert racing a sub-agent write can wedge it.

Sequencing (owner, 2026-09-21): lands AFTER plan B item 4 (docs/plans/2026-09-20 - 02, which rewrites undo.Mutation / entry.apply onto security.Fence) — never inside it. Needs its own design; inputs: pop AND close the group under the lock (else a racing Record appends to the group being walked); bump generation at pop time so plan B item 6's previewed 'apogee undo confirm <generation>' misses a second confirm; walk lock-free; re-lock for the redo push and persist(); the conflict rule (pre-image compared before overwrite) becomes a statement about WHEN it is compared. The audit's one-liner ('snapshot the group pointer, walk lock-free') is thinner than this. Candidate for /improve-codebase-architecture or a plan E after plan B archives.
close_reason: Closed

title: Undo pre-image snapshot git runs inside the workspace box on confined Auto writes (index.lock Permission denied)
description: Every write_file / edit_existing_file Run in Auto + confine-to-workspace on a landlock host paints 'undo: capture the pre-image of <ws>: apogee: snapshot: capture: git write-tree: exit 128: fatal: Unable to create <home>/snapshots/<session>/index.lock: Permission denied'. Root cause: executeRun (internal/agent/dispatch.go ~L908) installs the Confinement handle for confineChildren Runs BEFORE executeTool, so 'floorCtx := ctx' (dispatch.go ~L1270, whose comment claims it is taken before the handle goes on) already carries it and journal.MarkPre(floorCtx) runs the snapshot store's git inside the workspace box, where <home>/snapshots is unwritable. Journal.Close's post image fails the same way. Undo whole-tree images (ADR 0074) have been broken in that cell since 43f07c6a (2026-09-07); Allow-Edits and Ask-Before are unaffected. Reproduced locally (OrbStack kernel, landlock available) via TestE2EAnnouncedWorkspaceThroughASymlink's final frame; on CI the two failed re-exec'd git spawns per write push that test past its 5s wait (5 of the last 11 red runs). Fix: derive floorCtx from a ctx WITHOUT the handle (strip it in executeTool, or take it in executeRun before WithConfinement) so apogee's bookkeeping git never runs inside the model's box while git_stage's child still does. Add a regression test that a confined Auto write leaves the journal with a pre image (or that no 'undo:' ErrorEvent is emitted).
acceptance_criteria: A confined Auto write on a landlock host emits no 'undo:' ErrorEvent and the journal holds a pre/post image; git_stage's own child stays confined; TestE2EAnnouncedWorkspaceThroughASymlink's frame carries no 'Permission denied'.

title: ⌃c⌃c mid-answer lost the whole session record
description: A quit requested while a worker was in flight exited without ever writing the session record: finishWorker's quitting branch returned tea.Quit before the idle flush, on the reasoning that the per-Turn snapshots had already captured every completed Turn. stepToBoundary only snapshots at StatusTurnComplete, so an Exchange the model answers in ONE Step emits no turnSnapshotMsg at all — a ⌃c⌃c during that first answer left nothing on disk and the conversation was gone. Surfaced as a CI flake: TestE2EPopupFramesLists quits straight after the reply's text lands, and on a loaded runner the keypress beat exchangeDoneMsg, so the relaunched /sessions browser found an empty store (run 34155743192).
design: finishWorker's quitting branch now runs the closing flush for a settled (stateIdle) end and defers the exit to pumpOrQuit, exactly as quit() does for a clean quit. Safe for the same reason the idle save is: the worker has unwound and the engine is the Update loop's again (C1). A quit landing on a loop fault still leaves the record where the last save put it.
acceptance_criteria: A ⌃c⌃c while the model is still answering leaves a resumable record; TestE2EQuitMidAnswerStillSavesTheSession (held reply via stubllm await gate) and TestModelDoesNotSaveWhileBusy both pin it.
close_reason: fixed in this run: finishWorker flushes the settled boundary before the deferred exit

title: winlabel: journal claims carry no per-run secret and liveness is PID-only
description:
Remainder of apogee-73s (audit docs/reviews/code-audit-2026-09-20.md, High 'a forgeable confinement journal drives the victim's next Recover/Retire to NULL-SACL or label-write arbitrary paths'). Plan 'docs/plans/archived/2026-09-22 - 00 - audit-design-findings-plan.md' item 11 shipped the Linux-provable half (isVolumeRoot applied to RootJudged entries; a foreign prior under an unexpected label is carried with a bounded life, never dropped or restored). Out of scope there by owner call (2026-09-22), beaded here:
(a) Per-run secret: journal claims (labels-<pid>.json under ~/.apogee/confinement) are read before judgePriors and trusted verbatim; prior_sddl is attacker-chosen. Write a per-run secret into the journal and into the labelled root's own state (or ACL/HMAC) and verify it before any SetSDDL or clear.
(b) Creation-time liveness: journal-owner liveness is PID-only, so a recycled PID reads live and a dead one can be impersonated. Pin liveness to process creation time (GetProcessTimes).
Where: internal/platform/winlabel/retire.go (revertibleRoots, restorablePriors, judgeEntries), walk_windows.go (revertJournal, judgePriors), journal.go, session.go. Windows only: verifiable only on a Windows runner (compile-check here with GOOS=windows go test -c -o /dev/null ./internal/platform/winlabel/).
close_reason: Resolved by 'winlabel-journal-trust-and-landlock-udp-proof-plan' (381aad92..1c0ffeb6): journal entries bind file identity (vol/fid) and Recover refuses a mismatch; owner liveness pinned to PID + process creation time; journal dir fenced as a protected box root.

title: Six tight wall-clock assertions in unit tests can fail on a loaded box
description:
The slow-box sweep of 2026-09-22 cured the TUI test kit (internal/tuitest, cmd/apogee e2e helpers). These are the wall-clock assertions left OUTSIDE it, each a hard upper bound or a fixed sleep that a loaded machine breaks. Several want a different assertion rather than a bigger number.

- internal/tools/network_funnel_test.go:982 — slack = 250ms on an 850ms ceiling around a real resolver swap, an httptest dial and a goroutine handoff under -race. The sibling at :910 (elapsed > 20*budget) makes the same claim safely; copy that shape.
- internal/doctext/pdf_test.go:486 — elapsed > 100ms proxying "the refusal is decided before the parser allocates". Measure the allocation (the file already does this in TestExtractPDF_RefusesAnInflateBomb), do not time it.
- internal/provider/reliability_test.go:192 — elapsed >= retry429BaseDelay (1s) bounds two real httptest round trips with no margin.
- internal/agent/promptslot_test.go:79 and :124, internal/agent/approvalqueue_test.go:224, internal/agent/approvalcache_test.go:156, internal/domain/promptslot_test.go:59, internal/tools/askqueue_test.go:71 — time.Sleep(20ms) "long enough for the second caller to be genuinely waiting". A fixed sleep asserting another goroutine has reached a blocking point is the assumption a loaded machine breaks; in the queue tests it can invert the expected ordering. Needs a synchronisation point, not a longer sleep.
- internal/filewatch/filewatch_unix_test.go:51 — Sleep(testSettle/3) to land a second write INSIDE a 150ms settle window; a descheduled goroutine misses it and the coalescing claim is not exercised.
- internal/reactions/command_test.go:129-130 and internal/userexec/userexec_test.go:129,137 — ~800ms of real margin around two /bin/sh cold starts and a process-group kill under -race.
- cmd/apogee/e2e_stream_test.go:70 streamReplyWait = 15s, derived from a measurement on one box; cmd/apogee/e2e_approval_test.go:413 promptly = 2s around a whole TUI round trip; cmd/apogee/e2e_newcomer_test.go:38,40 (15m whole / 60s per step, with a local judge model and a docker exec).

Requirement behind all of them: the suite must pass on a slow CI runner or a slow developer machine. See docs/handoffs/2026-09-22 - 00 - ci-and-test-failures-triage.md.
acceptance_criteria: Each row either asserts the thing directly (allocation, a synchronisation point) or carries a budget generous enough for a loaded box; none is re-centred on one machine's measurement.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Airic Lenz
comments.text:
Verified fixed in the tree at 533ce9af. Every row the description enumerates is accounted for — by plan items 8-13, not only by item 10. Row by row:

1. internal/tools/network_funnel_test.go (was :982, the 250ms slack on an 850ms ceiling) — f623600a. The fixed slack is gone: the constants scaled (budget 2s, lookup 1.6s = 0.8*budget) and the ceiling is now a MULTIPLE of the budget, 'budget + budget/2', which sits strictly between the shared-budget outcome (~budget) and the per-phase one (lookup+budget). A floor assertion 'elapsed < lookup' was added so the case cannot pass without exercising the pre-flight. The comment states that room for a loaded box comes from scaling both constants, not from widening the slack.

2. internal/doctext/pdf_test.go (was :486, elapsed > 100ms) — f623600a. No longer timed. TestExtractPDF_RefusesAnOversizedXrefTable now measures runtime.MemStats TotalAlloc across the refusal against an 8 MiB ceiling, the same shape the inflate-bomb case already used, and is serial (no t.Parallel) so no sibling's allocations land in the delta. The comment records that the wall clock only ever stood in for the allocation.

3. internal/provider/reliability_test.go (was :192, elapsed >= retry429BaseDelay) — f623600a. Now asserts the gap the SERVER saw between the two request arrivals, 'arrivals[1].Sub(arrivals[0]) >= retry429BaseDelay', which excludes client-side round-trip overhead entirely instead of bounding it with no margin.

4. The six time.Sleep(20ms) 'long enough for the second caller to be genuinely waiting' sites — cddb5bbc and 32b984a5 (plan items 8 and 9). domain.PromptSlot gained Waiting(), counting callers inside Acquire, and all six sites now block on the waiter count instead: waitForPromptSlotWaiters (internal/domain/promptslot_test.go:59), waitForQueuedCallers (internal/agent/promptslot_test.go:79 and :124, approvalqueue_test.go:227, approvalcache_test.go:159), waitForQueuedAskers (internal/tools/askqueue_test.go:74). The seam itself is pinned by TestPromptSlot_WaitingCountsACallerUntilItIsAdmitted and TestPromptSlot_WaitingDropsWhenAQueuedCallerIsCancelled. The only time.Sleep left in approvalqueue_test.go is the fake approver's deliberate hold window, which is the thing being simulated rather than a synchronisation assumption.

5. internal/filewatch/filewatch_unix_test.go (Sleep(testSettle/3) into a 150ms settle window) — 3a1198d2. testSettle 150ms -> 500ms, so the fraction the test has to land inside is ~167ms rather than 50ms; the stalling child's margin also derives from testSettle ('testSettle + testSettle/2') so it stays proportional. filewatch_test.go records why the constants relate as they do.

6. internal/reactions/command_test.go and internal/userexec/userexec_test.go — 3a1198d2. The ~1s margins became a named 'const margin = 5 * time.Second' in both tables, and the scripts sleep 30 instead of 5 so the margin stays well under the thing it must not reach. Both comments state that the margin is the instrument, never the claim.

7. The e2e budgets outside the cured kit — 7ba67ced and 383c4f15. e2e_stream_test.go: streamReplyWait is no longer a 15s measurement but is DERIVED, 'tuitest.DefaultTimeout + runes*streamRuneAllowance', shared by the in-process test, its pty twin and the judge so the twins cannot drift. e2e_approval_test.go: 'promptly' is now 20 * settled (5s) off the kit's own unit instead of a raw 2s. e2e_newcomer_test.go: newcomerStepBudget 60s -> 3 minutes, admitting an apt-get, a domestic-link download or a build from source on a four-core ARM box, and newcomerBudget is derived from it ('newcomerMaxSteps * (step + judge allowance)') rather than chosen beside it — the note records that the old 15m could not fit even its own 20 x 60s of steps.

Packages re-run green unraced on this box (doctext, provider, filewatch, userexec, reactions; the cmd/apogee rows under apogee-61g).

Acceptance met: each row either asserts the thing directly (an allocation, a waiter count, a server-side gap) or carries a budget derived from a kit constant or a multiple of the thing it bounds; none is re-centred on one machine's measurement.

title: probemodel's 60s per battery call calls a slow local model hung
description:
cmd/apogee/probemodel.go:22 batteryRequestTimeout = 60 * time.Second per battery call. The comment's premise is the bug: "a call still running after a minute is a hung server rather than a slow model". On a 30B-class model quantised onto CPU — the hardware this product is built for — one short exchange of prefill plus generation past sixty seconds is ordinary.

Found by the slow-box deadline sweep, 2026-09-22.
acceptance_criteria: A slow local model completes the battery; the budget is sized for CPU inference or made configurable.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Airic Lenz
comments.text:
Verified fixed in the tree at 533ce9af (slow-box-deadlines plan, item 7, commit 297535bb).

- cmd/apogee/probemodel.go: batteryRequestTimeout 60s -> 300s, and it is now the DEFAULT rather than the bound — 'apogee probe model --timeout' overrides it (flags.DurationVar at the command's flag set).
- The comment whose premise was the bug is rewritten. It no longer claims 'a call still running after a minute is a hung server rather than a slow model'; it now says the servers this probe exists for are the slow ones, that a 30B-class model quantised onto CPU ordinarily spends minutes on a single short exchange, and that cutting that off would report a healthy server as broken. It also states what the budget is NOT: not a bound on the command and not a bound on one battery call, since a timed-out attempt is retryable and the client's retries multiply it by the attempt budget.
- Covered by cmd/apogee/probemodel_test.go; docs/manual/probe.md documents the flag.

Acceptance met: sized for CPU inference AND made configurable.

title: Execution-tool timeouts are unreachable on slow hardware: run_tests is a hard 5m, subprocess caps at 10m
description:
internal/tools/run_tests.go:46 runTestsTimeout = 300 * time.Second is hard-coded (used at :276, quoted at :427) with no way for the model or the user to ask for more — apogee's own suite on a Pi-class machine exceeds five minutes, so the model just gets "— timed out after 5m0s".

internal/subprocess/subprocess.go:28 MaxSubprocessTimeout = 600 * time.Second is a hard CEILING on a caller-named timeout (default 120s at :26), so a cold `go build ./...`, a `pip install` or a container build on a throttled laptop is unreachable through the execution tools at any requested timeout.

Found by the slow-box deadline sweep, 2026-09-22.
acceptance_criteria: run_tests takes a timeout (or reads one from config); the subprocess ceiling is raised or made configurable. A slow machine makes a build slower, not impossible.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Airic Lenz
comments.text:
Verified fixed in the tree at 533ce9af (slow-box-deadlines plan, items 5 and 6, commits e262100a and 218c266c). Both halves.

- internal/tools/run_tests.go: the hard 5m is gone. runTestsTimeout = 900 * time.Second is now only the DEFAULT when the model names no budget, and the tool takes a timeout_seconds argument. runTestsBudget() falls back to the tool's own default on absent/zero (never to the 120s subprocess default a zero Timeout would otherwise select) and hands a positive value through untouched, because internal/subprocess is the single place the ceiling is applied. The schema description is RENDERED from the default and the ceiling, so the model is told both numbers and told to raise the budget rather than re-run a timed-out suite.
- internal/subprocess/subprocess.go: MaxSubprocessTimeout 600s -> 3600s, so a cold 'go build ./...', a pip install or a container build is reachable at a requested timeout. python_exec.go and terminal.go quote the new ceiling; docs/manual/reactions.md dropped the 600s clamp sentence.

Acceptance met: a slow machine makes a build slower, not impossible.

title: A 10s bwrap probe that times out reports confinement unavailable for the whole session
description:
internal/platform/namespace_linux.go:111 namespaceProbeTimeout = 10 * time.Second bounds one real bwrap launch at startup. On expiry the result is "bwrap timed out" — confinement is reported unavailable for the entire session, i.e. a silently weaker sandbox. A cold-cache namespace setup on a loaded box is exactly the case that exceeds it.

Found by the slow-box deadline sweep, 2026-09-22.
acceptance_criteria: A slow probe does not downgrade the sandbox; either the budget is generous enough for a cold start, or a timeout is reported distinctly from an unavailable bwrap.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Airic Lenz
comments.text:
Verified fixed in the tree at 533ce9af (slow-box-deadlines plan, items 3 and 4, commits 255be681 and 66af40ba). Both halves of the acceptance landed, not just one.

- internal/platform/namespace_linux.go: namespaceProbeTimeout 10s -> 60s, with the reasoning recorded (the budget is only spent on a host that is failing to answer, so a generous ceiling costs a healthy host nothing; a Pi paging its first bwrap off an SD card stops being told it cannot fence when it can). Acceptance met.

title: esc stop: the disarm tick is unversioned, so a late tick can disarm a fresher arm
description:
Found while diagnosing the cmd/apogee load flake (TestE2EStreamCancelKeepsWhatArrived), 2026-09-22.

internal/tui/model.go:1612-1613 arms the esc stop by setting m.lastEsc = now and scheduling tea.Tick(escStopWindow, ... escStopResetMsg{}). The message carries no generation or stamp, and model.go:1031-1035 zeroes m.lastEsc for ANY escStopResetMsg it folds. So a tick scheduled for arm N but delivered late - which a backed-up fold queue causes - clears a FRESHER arm N+1 that was set in the meantime, and the user's second press then re-arms instead of confirming. ctrlCResetMsg has the same shape and the same hazard.

Note also that the window is measured at fold time (now := time.Now() at model.go:1603 runs when the KeyPressMsg is dequeued), so two presses well inside a second in the user's fingers do not stop the run if the second sits behind a backlog longer than escStopWindow.

Not a regression: the stop path is byte-identical at 1e112316, e2f3b944, 2327276a and HEAD (verified by hashing handleKey's esc case, the claim walk and finishWorker).

User-visible effect: under heavy load, esc x2 can silently fail to stop an in-flight turn; the hint stays up and a third press is needed. The driven tests no longer notice this because cmd/apogee's stopRun helper re-presses, so the register is now the only record.

Possible fix: stamp escStopResetMsg (and ctrlCResetMsg) with the arm it belongs to and ignore a tick whose stamp is stale.

title: session-snapshot ingestion restores untrusted history as committed conversation (audit 2026-09-20 Medium)
description:
Source: docs/reviews/code-audit-2026-09-20.md, Medium 'session-snapshot ingestion restores untrusted history as committed conversation'.
Where: internal/agent/state.go:157 (restoreState/decodeState), both ingestion paths (Resume / RestoreSession).

title: winlabel: a forgeable confinement journal drives the next Recover/Retire to NULL-SACL or label-write arbitrary paths (audit 2026-09-20 High)
description:
Source: docs/reviews/code-audit-2026-09-20.md, High 'a forgeable confinement journal drives the victim's next Recover/Retire to NULL-SACL or label-write arbitrary paths'. Windows only.
Where: internal/platform/winlabel/retire.go:210,257 (revertibleRoots/restorablePriors), walk_windows.go:400 (revertJournal), session.go:221.
What: journal claims are read before judgePriors and never guarded by a per-run secret; prior_sddl is attacker-chosen verbatim (only the path's current label is checked); liveness is PID-only (a handoff drops PID, so the claim later reads pid == 0 -> dead); the persisted RootJudged flag skips isVolumeRoot entirely. A planted labels-<pid>.json under ~/.apogee/confinement makes the next NewConfiner's Recover NULL-SACL an arbitrary tree or SetSDDL an arbitrary descriptor. Trigger needs same-user write into ~/.apogee/confinement (unconfined-mode model, compromised local MCP server); damage is label manipulation/DoS, no privilege boundary crossed. Also the priorRestorable inversion: only a current Low label makes a foreign prior restorable, any other label drops it permanently.
Audit fix: per-run secret written into the journal and into the labelled root's own state (or ACL/HMAC), verified before any SetSDDL/clear; apply isVolumeRoot even to RootJudged entries (the flag skips the label re-read, never the guardrail); pin liveness to process creation time (GetProcessTimes). Design together with the sibling stranded-label bead — same files.

title: winlabel: two confining sessions each spare the shared root, then strand the Low label unrecoverably (audit 2026-09-20 High)

Where: internal/platform/winlabel/retire.go:218, walk_windows.go:445-447, journal.go:341-344.
What: two sessions confining one workspace — each revertibleRoots gates on the sibling's PID being alive, so each spares the shared root to the other and deletes its own journal; both files gone while the Low label stays on disk. title: Upstream stream stall / in-band 504: one fixed re-stream, no idle timeout, faulted delegate loses its whole context
description:
Observed 2026-09-20 in session 20260920T120456Z-82db7883 (openrouter-ds4, deepseek-v4-flash via provider Relace, every call 3-8 min): sub-agent "L1 internal-floor-2" had done 34 tool calls / 13 turns / ~2.3M prompt tokens over 55 min when its next streaming call sat 520 s with no tokens and the wire returned an in-band error chunk {"choices":[],"error":{"code":504,"message":"Upstream idle timeout exceeded"}}. apogee surfaced `loop: apogee: upstream in-band error 504 ...`, the delegate faulted (`sub-agent faulted before finishing the delegated task: ...`), no receipt reached the parent and the child's conversation was discarded. Only the draft findings file the skill prompt had told it to write early survived.

Why apogee could not ride it out:
- HTTP retries (internal/provider/client.go:440-487, maxRetries=2, 200ms/1s base, Retry-After<=30s) cover 429/5xx/transport faults BEFORE the first byte only. Streaming (stream.go:100) has no per-attempt timeout and no inter-chunk idle timeout (stream.go:80-81, pinned by stream_test.go:1023) — a silent stream waits for the aggregator's cut.
- The in-band 504 is classified Retryable (fault.go:53-67, stream.go:201-213), but the loop allows exactly ONE re-stream per Turn after a fixed 1 s hold-off (loop.go:425-457 restreamSpent, restreamHoldoff loop.go:362); the second fault of any class goes emitLoopFault -> turnFailed -> endAbandoned (turn.go:183-199).
- A faulted delegate is not retained: retention + foldForParent run only under res.StepCapped (subagent.go:1043-1053, agent.go:900); `continue` after a fault answers unknownContinueResult (subagent.go:898-903, :184). The child's conv is still intact in memory when the Exchange closes Faulted — it is thrown away only when runSubAgent returns.
- No config key exists for retry count, request timeout or stream idle timeout (only judge/probe/title pass WithRequestTimeout/WithMaxRetries).

Proposed shape (each its own item; A and C are the minimum):
A. Stream idle timeout (`stream-idle-timeout`, generous default, reasoning deltas count as activity) that cuts a silent body read as a Retryable transient, plus a small re-stream budget (2-3) with exponential hold-off replacing the single restreamSpent latch.
B. Retain a faulted delegate the way a capped one is retained — fold via foldForParent (or keep the raw []domain.Message so `continue` re-seeds without re-spending the tokens) and add the continue line to the fault result.
C. Fault result names a surviving draft when output_path exists on disk (`[draft output at %s written before the fault]`), same note slot the cap path uses.

Invariants: engine-side only (ADR 0031); nothing new in front of the model beyond the continue/draft lines the cap path already ships; Bypass-neutral. Related: ADR 0018 (overflow fold + one retry), ADR 0046 (cap retry latch), ADR 0078 (fault classes); apogee-2un (finished siblings lost on cancel — the pool commits only after the group joins, dispatch.go:398-408) is the neighbouring loss and stays its own bead.

title: dangerous-action guard refuses read-only shell commands that name .git/hooks or .git/config
description:
The write-git-control-plane rule (internal/security/rules.go:143, pattern `\.git/(?:hooks|config|modules)\b`, WritesOnly) refuses ANY `terminal` command whose text mentions those paths, because a tool that declares no read-source keys is fully inspected (internal/security/dangerous.go:159). Reads are caught with the writes.

Observed 2026-09-14 in the /code-audit run (session 20260914T103923Z-50e9123c), two lens sub-agents refused with "write or delete under a repository's git control plane":

  ls -la .git/hooks/ 2>/dev/null | head -30; cmp -s .beads/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && echo BYTE-IDENTICAL || echo DIFFERENT
  cmp -s /workspace/repos/apogee/.git/hooks/commit-msg /workspace/repos/apogee/.beads/hooks/commit-msg && echo IDENTICAL || echo DIFFERENT; ls -l /workspace/repos/apogee/.git/hooks/commit-msg

Both are pure reads, and apogee's own AGENTS.md invites exactly this check ("`.git/hooks/commit-msg` is a deliberate dormant fallback — byte-identical to `.beads/hooks/commit-msg`"). The rule's own comment says it guards "the write that plants delayed execution, not the read", but for shell that intent is unimplemented: WritesOnly only narrows the view for tools that declare read sources.

Why it matters: an auditing or refocusing agent that inspects hooks is stopped by a hard refuse (no approval route), and the refusal reason misdescribes what it did. The floor invariant (nothing apogee puts in front of a model may make it worse than the bare loop) is what a false hard refuse chips at.

What to do: give the write-shaped view a notion of verb for shell text — e.g. only match a control-plane path when the command also carries a write/delete/redirect verb (`>`, `>>`, `tee`, `cp`/`mv`/`install` with the path as destination, `rm`, `chmod`, `git config --local/--global set`, `sed -i`, heredoc), or conversely skip the rule when every command in the pipeline is from a read-only set (`ls`, `cat`, `cmp`, `diff`, `head`, `tail`, `stat`, `file`, `grep`, `wc`, `md5sum`, `sha256sum`). Keep the hard refuse for anything ambiguous. Same question applies to the ssh-key and credential-file WritesOnly rules on shell text. Add guard tests for both refused commands above (must pass) and for `cp x .git/hooks/pre-commit`, `echo … > .git/config` (must still refuse).

title: internal/tools: TestConsoleClose_ReturnsTheUnreadTailAndTheExitCode flakes under shard load
description:
During a make check (the sharded suite, scripts/test-shards.sh, several packages running beside each other under -race) internal/tools TestConsoleClose_ReturnsTheUnreadTailAndTheExitCode failed once with 'console_close_test.go:56: result = "exited with code 3", want the output nobody had read yet'; it passes 5/5 in isolation and the package had not been touched — a load-sensitive test.

Reproduction (2026-09-14): go test -race -count=20..60 -run TestConsoleClose_ReturnsTheUnreadTailAndTheExitCode ./internal/tools/ while go test -race -count=1 ./cmd/apogee/ runs beside it fails 0-2 of 20 (1 of 60 in the bite check), same message; seen once at count=20 in isolation too.

Root cause: a TEST race, not a product one. The test helper openUndrainedConsole (console_read_test.go) opened the Console with wait_ms=-1 believing that meant 'no collection at all', but consoleWait maps a negative wait to a ZERO window, and console_open's collectConsoleWindow(0) still does one Read(0) that drains whatever the program has already printed. Under -race and host load the parent goroutine is descheduled between pty start and that read while the child shell (a separate process) runs ahead and prints 'tail-bytes', so the open call consumed the very tail the close was supposed to return; close then reported only 'exited with code 3'. The product contract holds (Close returns everything unread AFTER the join with the reader: process.Close joins readerDone before the tail is taken).

Fix: openUndrainedConsole now prefixes the command with 'read release; ' so the shell blocks on its terminal until the open call has returned, then types the newline that releases it — nothing the command prints can predate the open, by construction. Same helper serves TestConsoleRead's dropped-bytes test. consoleWait's comment sharpened ('waits for nothing; still reports what is already buffered'). Bite check: old helper fails 1/60 under the load reproduction; fixed helper 0/60 + 0/20 under the same load.
close_reason: fixed in b52dcebe

title: Confinement denial label blames writes for a non-write EPERM (ps fails in the sandbox)
description:
A sub-agent's `ps` call failed inside apogee's confinement with "Operation not permitted". Likely cause (unverified): /bin/ps is setuid-root here, and a setuid exec under no_new_privs / the confinement backend is refused — or ps's /proc access is refused; which backend was active is not recorded.

The denial watch (internal/platform/denialkill.go, denialLinePattern) matches any line ending in strerror(EPERM), and both labels in internal/tools/exec_common.go (confinementDenialLabel, confinementDenialStopLabel) then tell the model "writes are allowed only inside <roots>". ps wrote nothing, so the label points the model at re-aiming a write that never happened — misleading, especially for a small model.

Impact observed: minor — it was an incidental check and the agent carried on.

Fix direction (to design): word the labels so they do not assert the denied operation was a write (e.g. name the writable roots as one fact among others, or say the sandbox refused an operation such as a write, a setuid/privileged exec or a process inspection); optionally confirm the ps cause and document it as a known confinement limit.

Acceptance: a confined run whose EPERM does not come from a write gets a label that does not claim a write was blocked; existing write-denial labelling still names the writable roots.

title: undo: a concurrent Close or MarkPre can interleave with a lock-free Revert/Redo walk and act on the popped group
description:
Item 1 of the 2026-09-22 audit-design-findings plan (commit 9f684b83) made Journal.Revert and Journal.Redo walk their step with the journal lock RELEASED: the group is popped, the boundary set and the generation bumped under one short hold, then the filesystem work runs lock-free (internal/undo/journal.go:465).

Before that, the whole step ran under one hold, so a concurrent snapshot call could not interleave with it. It now can: Journal.Close (internal/undo/snapshot.go:124) and Journal.MarkPre (internal/undo/snapshot.go:76) take the lock in the window where the reverted group is already popped, so a Close arriving mid-walk acts on the PREVIOUS group rather than the one being walked.

Harmless today because /undo and /redo are idle-only (ADR 0051 decision 7), so no snapshot call is in flight while a walk runs; taking the Close/MarkPre holds into the new lock discipline was declared out of scope by item 1. Worth closing before anything makes a revert concurrent with a live exchange.

title: gitexec: a root that is no repository memoises its command-config answer on no prints, so a repo git init-ed under it mid-session is served the pre-init answer until restart
description:

A root that is no repository yields no file from `git rev-parse --git-path`, so its memoised answer carries no fileprints and `commandConfigProbe.holds()` holds trivially for the process lifetime (internal/gitexec/gitexec.go:402-411, the 'No prints at all … holds trivially' rule; the cache hit at internal/gitexec/gitexec.go:463). A repository `git init`-ed under such a root mid-session and then given a command-valued key (`filter.<x>.clean`, `diff.<x>.textconv`, …) is therefore still served the pre-init clean answer until apogee restarts, and the next git tool runs it.

This is the plan's own rule — no `.git/` path is assumed, a `GIT_DIR`-redirected run is judged by its own store — and the fake-git memo test in internal/gitexec/gitexec_test.go depends on the no-prints answer memoising. Closing it needs an assumed `<root>/.git` print (or a print of the root directory itself) that the rule forbids; the design call is the owner's.

Behaviour is unchanged from before the run for this case (the memo was once-per-process for every root); the repository case is closed by 4e394d43.

title: writeTarget.note() discloses the workspace's own symlink on every write (macOS)
description:
writeTarget.note() (internal/tools/write_target.go:179) returns " → resolves to <Real>" whenever Real != Named, verbatim. Named is root-joined from the argument with nothing followed; Real is security.EvalRealPath of that (resolveTargetUnbounded, internal/tools/workspace_scoped.go:207). The root itself is never resolved — resolveRoots (cmd/apogee/wire.go:428) only makes it absolute — so a workspace reached through ANY symlink puts the note on EVERY write, not just the one that went somewhere else.

On macOS that is the common case, not the edge: `cd /tmp/x && apogee` keeps PWD as /tmp/x while the real path is /private/tmp/x, so every write_file/edit result the model reads grows " → resolves to /private/tmp/x/…". Cosmetic — the write lands where it should and the fence judges Real — but it defeats the note's own contract ("nothing on the common path", "naming where the call really landed when that is NOT the path the argument named") and dilutes the one disclosure that matters, the per-file symlink.

Surfaced 2026-09-18 while making the suite green on macOS: TestWriteTargetNote had to take its root by real path (commit c468a53b) to test what it claims.

Fix sketch: compare Real against the argument resolved under the ROOT's real path — i.e. note only when EvalRealPath(named) != EvalRealPath(root)+rel — or resolve the root once at scope construction (writeScopeOf) so Named already carries the real root. Either way the approval pane and the note must keep agreeing (the "compute it BEFORE the write" rule at note()); check TestWriteTargetNote's symlinked-final-name case still discloses.

title: Headless text output is rendered live from the Event stream
description:
Follow-up from the apogee-tvw grill (2026-09-07), owner-approved at grill Q4.

Today `apogee headless` prints NOTHING until the run completes: the answer is one Fprintln of run.Result.FinalText (cmd/apogee/headless.go:642) and the surrounding block is composed post-hoc from the same run.Result (headless.go:635-677). A ten-minute run looks hung.

Once apogee-tvw lands, `--format text` and `--format json` could become two renderers over one Event stream, giving headless live output — the opencode shape.

Deliberately NOT taken into apogee-tvw: its acceptance criterion is 'the human-readable default output is unchanged', and a live renderer cannot reproduce a post-hoc summary that prints run.Result-only facts (Wrote, UndoNote, ContextFiles, per-sub-agent fills) in summary order without buffering to the end. It is cheaper to build AFTER the Event stream exists.
acceptance_criteria: apogee headless --format text emits output as the run progresses rather than only at completion; the facts that exist only on run.Result still appear, in their current wording, at the end.

title: Make the e2e tests genuinely parallel (t.Setenv + CheckLeaks)
description:
Process sharding (scripts/test-shards.sh) works around two constraints rather than removing them. Removing them would let the 189 serial tests in cmd/apogee and the 1267 in internal/tui overlap inside one process, on top of the sharding:

1. `assertNoAmbientApogeeConfig` (cmd/apogee/e2e_support_test.go:542) calls `t.Setenv` on six APOGEE_* vars; the testing package panics if a test uses both t.Setenv and t.Parallel. Measured baseline for whoever picks this up: cmd/apogee 189 serial tests / 168.1s vs 404 parallel tests / 5.0s; internal/tui 1267 / 98.3s vs 498 / 3.8s.
acceptance_criteria: The e2e tests run with t.Parallel without false leak reports, and the suite is measurably faster than sharding alone.

title: The published binaries are not code-signed
description:
**Status:** parked 2026-08-05, the day the first prebuilt binaries shipped (v0.11.0 — all six
targets as release assets, plus the `airiclenz/tap` Homebrew formula that installs them). The
README states the gap where the download is rather than burying it, so this entry exists to keep
that statement honest and to hold the design once it is picked up.

**What the gap actually is, per platform** — it is two different problems wearing one name:

- **macOS.** The Go linker already ad-hoc signs `darwin/arm64` (verified on the v0.11.0 asset:
  `LC_CODE_SIGNATURE`, 162 KB), which is the *load* requirement on Apple Silicon — without it the
  kernel SIGKILLs the process, so the binaries do run. What is missing is **Developer ID signing +
  notarisation**, which is the *Gatekeeper* requirement: a browser download carries
  `com.apple.quarantine` and is refused until `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine` clears it. A `curl`
  download never sets the attribute, and Homebrew's own download does not either — so the brew path
  and the documented `curl` path are both unaffected today. Only the browser path is.
  `darwin/amd64` carries no signature and needs none to load.
- **Windows.** No signature at all, so SmartScreen warns about an unrecognised publisher. An
  Authenticode certificate is the only fix, and reputation accrues per-certificate over time.

**Why it is deferred, not dropped.** Both halves cost money and identity, not engineering: an Apple
Developer Program membership (notarisation also needs a per-release upload to Apple's service, so
it puts a network round-trip and a credential into `make dist`'s path) and an Authenticode
certificate from a CA. Neither belongs in a pre-production 0.x release cut from a laptop, and
`SHA256SUMS` — published as a release asset, and what the Homebrew formula pins per platform — is
the integrity check that is actually available today.

**The design question to settle when this is picked up:** whether signing stays a *release-time*
step layered over `make dist` (the target keeps producing unsigned archives, and a separate
signing/notarisation pass rewrites them before upload) or moves *into* it. The layered answer is
strongly preferred: `make dist` is cross-platform by construction — one CGO-free `go build` per
target from whichever machine cuts the release — whereas `codesign`/`notarytool` run only on macOS
and `signtool` only on Windows. Folding either in would make the whole matrix un-buildable from a
single host, which is the property the target exists to have. That points at CI (a signing job per
platform, secrets held there) rather than at the Makefile, and CI-cut releases are not a thing this
repo does yet — settle that first.

title: Windows Auto: box-local %TEMP% / toolchain caches
description:
**Status:** recorded 2026-07-22 (Phase 5 review fixes,
`docs/plans/archived/2026-07-22 - 02 - phase5-review-fixes-plan.md` item 12). Not built by that
plan by decision — it needs its own design session. Sources: ADR 0020 §2 (the "Consequence for the
box builder" paragraph) and `docs/design/confinement-execution-contract.md` §7.

**The gap.** ADR 0020 §2 names the toolchain's cache/temp dirs a **hard prerequisite** on Windows,
not the ergonomic nicety contract §7 treats them as on Linux/macOS: the confined child runs under a
*low-integrity* token, and a Low process cannot write to an unlabelled (Medium) directory at all.
`%TEMP%`, `$GOCACHE`, `~/.npm`, `~/.cargo` and the pip cache all live outside the workspace and are
unlabelled, so under the Windows fence a confined `go build`, `go test`, `pip install` or `npm ci`
fails outright — not with a partial result, but at the first write to its cache or temp dir. The
workspace-scoped writes the fence does cover work fine; toolchain work under Auto does not.

**Why nothing bridges it today.** The box field that would carry those dirs,
`domain.Config.ConfineWritablePaths`, has only **readers** —
`internal/agent/dispatch.go:417` and `:457`, which copy it into
`domain.ConfinementBox.WritablePaths` for a tool call and for a hook-time subprocess respectively —
and, repo-wide, **no writer**: nothing probes for toolchain caches and nothing surfaces the field in
config, so it is always empty. Contract §7's own recommendation ("seed `WritablePaths` with the
detected toolchain cache + temp dirs by default, probed, not hard-coded") was never implemented on
any platform; on Windows it is the difference between a usable fence and an unusable one.
`internal/platform`'s `ScopeEnv` (the environment-scoping seam ADR 0020 §2 points at) exists and is
used by `git` and the Go toolchain, but `terminal` and `python_exec` inherit the user's `%TEMP%`
unchanged.

**The design question to settle when this is picked up:** a **box-local `%TEMP%`** — point the
confined child's `TMP`/`TEMP` (and `GOTMPDIR`, `GOCACHE`, …) at a labelled directory inside the box
via `ScopeEnv`, so nothing outside the workspace is ever marked — **versus labelling the user's own
cache/temp trees**, which is simpler but marks large, long-lived, shared trees Low (ADR 0020's own
"keep the labelled surface small" argument, and the ~1 ms-per-object walk cost, both cut against
it). ADR 0020 §2 already prefers the box-local answer, and calls it environment-scoped execution
plus box construction, **not** a `Confine` responsibility — so the work lands in the box builder and
the execution tools, and the `Confine` contract (§2) is unaffected. Whichever way it goes, it also
decides whether cache dirs are *probed* per toolchain or named in config, and it is the natural
moment to give `ConfineWritablePaths` its first writer.

title: Adaptive prompt complexity — request slimming driven by the capability tier
description:
**Status:** parked 2026-07-22 by decision, not by omission
([ADR 0021](docs/adr/0021-probe-is-two-halves-the-host-report-is-free-the-model-battery-is-an-explicit-act.md)
Q3; `../apogee-sim/mission.md` item 2). Phase 5 ships the **capability tier** as a reported
`apogee probe model` field and stops there.

The idea: a pre-request transform that shapes the outgoing request to what the model can
actually digest — stripping tool descriptions down to names and one line, shortening the system
prompt, simplifying output formatting — selected by the tier the probe observed. It is the
mission's "prompt complexity tier" and aims squarely at the smallest models, the ones this
project exists for.

Why it is not built with the probe: this is model-facing behaviour inside the loop, so it is a
**lab row** on the Mechanism registry — earning its place per model on the non-inferiority gate
against Bypass, with a Table B bench-validation entry
([ADR 0009](docs/adr/0009-the-ab-decision-rule.md); the Phase-5 settled design: nothing
model-facing ships default-on without bench evidence) — or, if the evidence turns out to hold for
every model, a **Floor guard**, which takes a verdict of its own under
[ADR 0071](docs/adr/0071-floor-guards-are-engine-behaviour-and-the-nudge-catalogue-retires.md).
Shipping it alongside the probe would mean an unvalidated transform in front of every model
either way. The tier signal costs nothing and is already there when the evidence is.

When picked up: build it as a **pre-request** transform, **off** until a stored probe record's tier
arms it (so it no-ops entirely for an un-probed model), and bench it on at least one small model
before it reaches anyone by default. Open design questions kept warm: whether slimming applies
per-request or per-session (a mid-session change of tool descriptions is a history-consistency
question), and whether the tier or the individual battery findings (native tool calls vs. JSON
vs. multi-step) are the better gate — the findings are strictly more informative, the tier is
strictly easier to reason about.

title: Configurable tool × mode security matrix
description:
**Status:** parked 2026-06-24 (Phase-3 grill). Post-v1, **additive** — config is additive,
so this is a minor bump, not a freeze break. Cross-reference: ADR 0049 (landed 2026-08-14) settled
the same dispatch-gate-vs-tool-level-fence seam — an approved out-of-workspace write executes
through a permit pinned to the disclosed target — and its floor constrains this design: the Gate is
the bound, an approval is final, and there is no hard-deny tier above it.

**The idea (owner, 2026-06-24):** let the user configure precisely how each tool behaves in
each mode — a `(tool × mode) → disposition` matrix surfaced in config.

**Why it's coherent:** the disposition table *already exists internally* — `needsApproval` /
D5 is exactly `(mode × tool-disposition) → {auto-run, confine, gate, deny}`. v1 ships it as an
explicit internal table; this feature would expose a *user-tunable* layer on top.

**The two constraints that make it safe + shippable (must hold when we build it):**

1. **Tighten-only (the law).** A user override may only make a cell **stricter** than its mode
   default (toward gate/deny) — **never looser**. Loosening a whole tool-class would silently
   dissolve a mode's guarantee (e.g. `terminal → Auto → allow, unconfined` reintroduces the
   "unsupervised *and* unbounded" hole ADR 0004/0012 forbid; `write_file → Plan → allow` breaks
   Plan's read-only promise). The **only** blanket loosen is `confine-to-workspace=false`, which
   is gated behind an explicit "I am the sandbox" acknowledgement. Narrow, explicit, opt-in
   loosens (a `NetworkAllow` host; a `terminal` command-pattern allowlist entry like `go build`,
   `npm test`) are fine — same shape as the per-project allowlist already in `ConfinementBox`.

2. **Freeze cost.** A per-tool×mode config block turns **every tool name into a frozen config
   key** and adds a sizable schema right at the `v1.0.0` cut (fights D7 — keep the v1 surface
   minimal). Deferring it past v1 avoids that; config additivity means it loses nothing by waiting.

**Related "approval-precision" knobs to design *together* with this (also parked):**
- **Command-pattern allowlist for `terminal`** — "auto-allow `go build` / `npm test`" without a
  prompt. This is the thing people usually *actually* want when they say "configure the tools";
  finer than tool-level. A narrow explicit loosen (constraint 1), so it's allowed.
- **Per-host `NetworkAllow` precision** — already a field on `ConfinementBox`; a UI/config layer
  to manage it per project belongs with the matrix.

**What v1 ships instead (so the deferral is safe):** the internal disposition table (D5) +
the `confine-to-workspace` flag (the one blanket loosen) + the existing narrow allowlists.

title: Test drivers — residue: the claims no driver observes
description:
**Status:** recorded 2026-08-28 at the close of the test-drivers kit plan
(`docs/plans/2026-08-27 - 02 - test-drivers-kit-plan.md`). **No open work.** These are the
accepted proxies ratified by
[ADR 0062](docs/adr/0062-test-drivers-are-drivers.md) decision 5, written down so a later reader
does not re-open them as coverage gaps.

The live source is the "which driver observes which claim" table in
[`docs/design/test-drivers.md`](docs/design/test-drivers.md). Its **Not observable** column names
two different things: most cells name the instrument that asserts the claim INSTEAD (a session
record, a request log, a unit test), and those are covered. Only the rows below are irreducible —
the claim leaves the machine, and the proxy beside it *is* what "that item passes" means.

- **Font tofu (T-20)** — whether the reader's own font carries the glyph at all. The emulator's
  cell width is the width authority (`TestE2EWidthTicksMultiSelectChoices`,
  `TestE2EWidthSurvivesAColourSchemeSwitch`); what a font does with a codepoint is outside every
  terminal apogee can drive.
- **Felt flicker (T-24)** — proxied by the `--tui-trace` repaint ceiling
  (`TestE2EStreamRepaintCeiling`): bytes written and full-frame repaints per streamed token,
  pinned against a ceiling. Nothing measures perception.
- **What a real desktop application does with the file (T-19)** — the hand-off is asserted at its
  argv through the `openerLookPath` seam (`TestE2EPresentOpensOnlyTheAllowedFormats`), and the
  refusals by that log's ABSENCE of a launch. The application on the other side is not apogee's.
- **`brew upgrade` before the release it upgrades to exists (T-21), and the Homebrew and
  OpenRouter steps of the newcomer walk (T-23)** — both need a PUBLISHED release, and the second
  a real API key. The post-publish half runs by hand as `make release-smoke VERSION=vX.Y.Z`
  (`scripts/release-smoke.sh`); the container walk (`TestNewcomerFollowsTheDocs`) judges
  everything that needs neither.
close_reason: Accepted proxies ratified by ADR 0062 decision 5, recorded so they are not re-opened as coverage gaps. Migrated from ISSUES.md 2026-09-03.

title: Model-facing skill discovery: B1 auto-attach — deferred by ADR 0061
description:

for B1**, and a bench arm against Bypass. **The reusable half exists:** `skills.Catalog.Suggest`
(plan `docs/plans/archived/2026-08-27 - 01 - skill-suggestions-band-plan.md`) is engine-level and
model-free, so B1 would consume the matcher rather than grow a second one — as `Catalog.Lookup`,
B2's half, now does.

title: A model-facing schedule tool — daemon-era, not v1
description:
**Status:** parked 2026-08-04 (assessment at the `/schedule` close-out,
[ADR 0033](docs/adr/0033-the-scheduler-is-a-library-and-the-tui-is-its-first-driver-surface.md)).
The question: should the model be able to create Schedules itself, via a tool, instead of telling
the human to run `/schedule`?

**Why not now — two costs, one thin benefit.** The benefit is a keystroke: a TUI-hosted Schedule
dies with the process, so the model would only ever set up something short-lived the human can
create with one command. Against that: (1) **catalogue dilution** — every schema costs context and
tool-selection accuracy for the 4B–35B target class, tools are not per-model curated the way a
lab Mechanism row is, and a tool relevant in one session in fifty is exactly what the never-worse
invariant says to refuse; (2) **authorization inversion** — ADR 0033 decision 3 makes the *human's*
creation choice the mode authorization, and a model-created Auto schedule is the model granting its
future self unattended runs; inside a Firing it is self-replication (a firing scheduling more
firings).

**The shape when built (so it is not re-derived).** Layering is *not* the blocker — the precedent
is `ask_user`: a driver-supplied delegate seam, nil = tool not registered, and
[ADR 0002](docs/adr/0002-tools-are-an-open-extension-point-mechanisms-are-curated.md)'s open
registry means the driver that owns the scheduler registers the tool without touching the engine.
Creation routes through the **Approver** as a gated (non-ReadOnly) action, which buys the key
property for free: a Firing's fail-safe denier refuses it, so self-replication is structurally
impossible with no special-casing, and Ask-Before preserves decision 3's human authorization at the
gate. The residual hole is Auto (gated-but-eligible runs unsupervised — the exact bad case):
"create an Auto schedule" belongs in the footgun-guard's dangerous tier, or the tool caps
model-creatable schedules at Plan. Sub-agents don't inherit it (ADR 0005).

**The trigger to pick it up: a real need.** Durable schedules that survive quit are where a model
setting up its own monitoring has real value, and the companion feature is the cross-session
approval surface ADR 0033 already named when it rejected Ask-Before schedules. Build the tool once,
at that layer; the TUI still never has to register it. The daemon's shape has since been settled —
[ADR 0034](docs/adr/0034-the-daemon-is-an-in-repo-subcommand-over-a-declarative-trigger-action-file.md),
an in-repo subcommand over a declarative trigger-action file — and `apogee daemon` itself shipped
on 2026-08-22, which made this tool possible, not needed. Re-parked 2026-08-22 (owner call): this
entry stays parked until a real need for a model-facing schedule tool appears.
**Not the vehicle:** MCP — schedules are
in-process driver state, Firings run without MCP, and ADR 0031 forbids first-party connectors.

description:

[ADR 0023](docs/adr/0023-the-system-prompt-is-a-configured-template-rendered-per-request.md)).
